review_status: Draft seed list for review by the question-bank curator. Add items rather than renaming ids already in use.

items.description: Moves a term to the other side of an equation without changing its sign
Uses the wrong inverse operation, for example subtracting a coefficient instead of dividing by it
Applies an operation to only one side, or only one term, of an equation
Multiplies only the first term inside a bracket
Does not change every sign when expanding a bracket preceded by a minus sign
Squares or multiplies binomials without the middle terms, for example (a + b)² = a² + b²
Combines unlike terms, such as x and x², or ab and a
Leaves a common factor inside the brackets, so the expression is not fully factorised
Chooses factor pairs with the wrong signs when factorising a quadratic
Misapplies the difference of two squares, for example factorising a² + b² or writing (a - b)²
Cancels individual terms instead of common factors in an algebraic fraction
Adds numerators and denominators separately or uses an incorrect common denominator
Multiplies only part of a numerator when writing fractions over a common denominator
Multiplies indices when multiplying powers, or adds indices when raising a power to a power
Treats a negative index as a negative number instead of a reciprocal
Confuses the root and the power in a fractional index
Applies a power to the variable but not the coefficient, for example (3x)² = 3x²
Factorises or uses the formula before rearranging the quadratic to equal zero
Makes a sign or bracket error when substituting into the quadratic formula
Gives x = a instead of x = -a from a factor (x + a) = 0
Adds equations when they should be subtracted, or the reverse, when eliminating a variable
Finds only one unknown or one root and stops
Does not reverse the inequality sign after multiplying or dividing by a negative number
Uses the wrong open or closed circle, or broken or solid line, for a strict or inclusive inequality
Shades the wanted region instead of the unwanted region, or describes the region with reversed inequalities
Uses the common difference as the nth term or omits the adjusting constant, for example 3n instead of 3n + 2
Confuses a term's value with its position in the sequence
Uses the given values directly without finding the constant of proportionality, or uses the wrong power
Treats inverse proportion as direct proportion
Calculates gradient as horizontal change over vertical change
Misreads the scale or a value on a graph axis
Uses the wrong area formula, or a gradient, for distance under a speed-time graph
Substitutes correctly but evaluates in the wrong order, for example -3² instead of (-3)²
Gives the reciprocal 1/f(x) instead of the inverse function, or reverses operations in the wrong order
Applies the functions in the wrong order for a composite function
Mixes units, such as dollars and cents, when forming an equation
Writes the stated relationship backwards when forming an expression or equation
Removes a square, square root or power in the wrong order when changing the subject
